extraction.name: Evaluating Object Hallucination in Large Vision-Language Models
extraction.description: This work presents the first systematic study on object hallucination of LVLMs. We conduct the evaluation experiments on several representative LVLMs... we further design a polling-based query method called POPE for better evaluation of object hallucination.
extraction.creator: Yifan Li, Yifan Du, Kun Zhou, Jinpeng Wang, Wayne Xin Zhao and Ji-Rong Wen
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset (POPE) is constructed by sampling images from existing datasets (MSCOCO, A-OKVQA, GQA) and generating polling questions based on ground-truth and nonexistent objects.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images and annotations are sourced from MSCOCO, A-OKVQA, and GQA datasets.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Questions are built using ground-truth objects for 'Yes' answers and negative sampling for 'No' answers, utilizing three strategies: Random Sampling, Popular Sampling, and Adversarial Sampling.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images were filtered to ensure they contained a minimum number of ground-truth objects before constructing a fixed number of questions per image.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Objects in the images are obtained either from existing human annotations or through automatic segmentation tools to build the polling questions.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Object hallucination in LVLMs can lead to unexpected consequences and serious safety issues in real-world deployments, such as autonomous driving.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset highlights biases in LVLMs where they tend to hallucinate objects that frequently appear or co-occur in the unbalanced visual instruction datasets (like MSCOCO) they were fine-tuned on.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Limitations include focusing only on object hallucination rather than overall capacity, evaluating only on a subset of validation sets due to compute limits, potential matching failures in LVLM responses, and inconsistencies between automatic segmentation labels and human annotations.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset (POPE) is used to evaluate the object hallucination problem in Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) via a binary classification polling task.

description.evidence: This work presents the first systematic study on object hallucination of LVLMs. We conduct the evaluation experiments on several representative LVLMs, and show that they mostly suffer from severe object hallucination issues. We further discuss that the visual instructions may influence the hallucination... Besides, we further design a polling-based query method called POPE for better evaluation of object hallucination.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: The hallucination phenomenon hinders the safe use of LVLMs in real-world deployment, as it may result in unexpected consequences caused by these hallucinated objects (MacLeod et al., 2017). For example, due to an incorrect understanding of the extemal environment, an autonomous driving system would make wrong decisions when encountering unexpected events, which might lead to serious safety issues.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: As the visual instruction datasets of these LVLMs are mostly constructed based on MSCOCO (Lin et al., 2014), they generally share a similar unbalanced object distribution where top frequent objects occupy a major part of the dataset. After being fine-tuned on them, LVLMs may also be prone to generate (or hallucinate) frequently appearing objects in MSCOCO.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: First, we only focus on the object hallucination problem in LVLMs, while do not consider other aspects that can reflect the capacities of LVLMs... Second, due to the limitation of computation resources, we have to evaluate all models on a part of the validation set for each dataset... Third, our proposed POPE utilizes a matching-based method to determine whether LVLMs answer “Yes” or “No”, while empirically, LVLMs may occasionally fail to provide answers explicitly containing these words... Fourth, when combined with the automatic segmentation tool, the objects would be annotated based on the label set by the tool, which may be inconsistent with the collected human annotations

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: POPE focuses on constructing a set of triples, each of which consists of an image, multiple questions and their answers... After constructing the evaluation triples, we can directly poll LVLMs with them and collect the predicted answers... to provide an improved evaluation approach for the object hallucination of LVLMs.
